original_test_intent: Physically verify that the designated liquid-cooling tray detects a controlled small PG25 leak, initiates the required local shutoff, and reports the exact expected BMC alarm without uncontrolled coolant exposure.
original_method: Approve tray/location/rate/duration, operating/power state, containment, and signal matrix; record physical and BMC baseline; have a qualified operator introduce one controlled drip; time detection and shutoff; capture physical plus BMC evidence; isolate coolant, clean, inspect, and restore under the hardware recovery plan.
manual_activity: Qualified hardware personnel prepare, introduce, observe, contain, clean, inspect, and restore the physical PG25 leak test; the owner reviews physical and BMC evidence.
required_inputs: Sensor/valve/pump/BMC signal matrix and timing limits
PPE, containment, spill response, cleanup, inspection, and recovery
safety_requirements: Stop on uncontrolled flow, delayed shutoff, missing alarm, or unsafe exposure
agent_execution_scope: Collect owner-approved procedure and asset mappings
Capture non-destructive BMC/SEL baseline if authorized
Perform no physical stimulus, visual claim, interlock bypass, cleanup, recovery decision, or DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Disposition anomaly and issue PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It correctly states that no command can create the physical leak, but lacks the exact manual stimulus and full physical/BMC evidence requirements.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No remote execution command; use the approved manual PG25 leak procedure and only read-only BMC evidence collection where authorized.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Slow PG25 dripping, tray detection, turn-off, correct BMC signals, no bundle, and 60/60-minute values remain.

modernized_recommendation.status: QUALIFIED MANUAL CONTROLLED PG25 LEAK TEST
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Pair controlled physical stimulus and response timing with immutable BMC signal evidence and documented containment/recovery.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines the missing stimulus envelope, identities, safety controls, and cleanup acceptance.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: BMC logs alone cannot prove the leak was controlled, physically detected, shut off, or safely contained.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Coolant can reach electronics, defeat containment, create slip/electrical hazards, or damage the tray and adjacent hardware.

project_override_considerations: Do not substitute simulated sensor input or logs for actual tray leak coverage unless an engineer explicitly creates a separate simulation testcase. Do not infer shutoff means valve, pump, tray power, or system power without the signal matrix.
expected_evidence: Timestamped physical stimulus, detection, shutoff, and containment evidence
Complete BMC/Redfish/SEL alarm identifiers and timing
Cleanup, exposure inspection, restored state, and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The short source is internally consistent but underspecified; missing leak parameters, signal identities, timing, and recovery are engineering prerequisites rather than contradictory source claims.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Static review is complete; a qualified operator and approved physical procedure can supply the missing execution inputs.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2093 Wistron-GB NV PVP HW-00017-V003: approve PG25 leak point/rate/duration and fixture, safe power/interlock state, tray/sensor/valve/pump mapping, expected BMC signal IDs and detection/shutoff times, PPE/containment, stop conditions, cleanup, inspection, and recovery.

review_improvement: Keeps the test fully manual while making its physical stimulus, shutoff behavior, BMC evidence, and coolant recovery auditable and safe.
independent_technical_reasoning: A leak alarm does not by itself prove the tray physically stopped the hazardous condition; detection latency, shutoff actuator/state, and containment must be observed at the hardware. PG25 volume and location determine whether the stimulus exercises the intended sensor without wetting electronics. Time-correlated BMC signals independently prove management reporting, while post-cleanup inspection establishes that the test did not leave latent coolant exposure.
